messages:
Maria (Support): Hey team — Acme reported a sudden spike in 401s and cross-region tail latency after we migrated their failover policy at 08:15 UTC. They saw requests hitting eu-west-1 even though primary is us-west-2.

Jordan (SRE): Can you drop the customer request ids or a sample trace?

Maria (Support): shared trace ids: r-7a2c, r-7a2d. Logs show 401s from auth service in eu-west-1. Latency from their app jumped to ~600ms. They said it started right after we applied the new weighted affinity migration.

Dev Support: Noted. I can repro locally by toggling the policy. Quick reproduction steps I used:
```bash
# call with no cookie (should sticky to primary)
curl -s -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -o /dev/null
# call with old cookie from primary (works)
curl -s -b "_rwd_affinity=primary; Path=/; Max-Age=3600" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
I then switched the policy to the new format and observed the cookie being treated as expired immediately.

Alex (Runtime Eng): Hmm — that sounds like the TTL unit conversion bug I hinted at in yesterday's deploy notes. The migration script converted ttl_percent -> ttl_seconds but for sticky cookies an extra offset of 30s was accidentally added for legacy entries. That would cause old cookies to look stale.

Lisa (Support Eng): If cookies are rejected, requests fall through to failover rules, which can route to secondary region if weights/priorities are misinterpreted. Did the migration also flip weight semantics?

Alex (Runtime Eng): Yes — two problems in one: weight fields in the legacy UI were 0-1 floats (e.g., 0.8) but in the new policy store they became integers 0-100 without normalization. The combination means some hosts ended up with priority inversion and the stale cookie triggered fallback to eu-west.

Jordan (SRE): Can you paste the policy dump for Acme?

Maria (Support): policy dump (sanitized):
```json
{
  "id": "policy-acme-42",
  "affinity_cookie_ttl": "30",  # legacy unit was minutes
  "failover": [
    {"region": "us-west-2", "weight": "80", "priority": 1},
    {"region": "eu-west-1", "weight": "20", "priority": 2}
  ]
}
```

Alex (Runtime Eng): There it is — affinity_cookie_ttl stored as "30" (legacy minutes) but runtime reads seconds, then applies the +30s migration offset, so cookie TTL effectively becomes 0 or negative for many clients. Also weights were ingested as strings and parsed differently, so eu-west ended up with higher effective weight for some hashed buckets.

Jordan (SRE): That explains both the wrong-region routing and auth 401s (because token binding was regional). How widespread is this? Any other customers showing similar patterns?

Dev Support: We've got 6 alerts in the last 2 hours for elevated 401s correlated to policy migration jobs: acme, greenleaf, pivotai. All had policies created before 2024-09.

Maria (Support): Customer impact: multiple 401s, latency, and an egress cost bump due to cross-region traffic. They are asking for immediate rollback and a postmortem.

Alex (Runtime Eng): Action plan: 1) Roll back the migration for pre-2024 policies to the previous storage format (hotfix). 2) Patch migration script to normalize weight floats -> percentage ints properly and remove the erroneous +30s offset. 3) Add a data validation step: if affinity_cookie_ttl <= 60 treat as minutes vs seconds heuristic and log a warning.

Jordan (SRE): I'll prepare a rollback runbook. Quick rollback commands:
```bash
# rollback migration for a single policy
redwoodctl policy set --id policy-acme-42 --raw-store 'legacy' --force
# confirm routing table
redwoodctl route dump --policy policy-acme-42 | jq .
```
I can run for Acme now if we agree.

Lisa (Support Eng): Also suggest temporary mitigations for affected customers: 1) issue short-lived API key rotation scoped to us-west-2, 2) set a per-customer routing override to pin to primary region until fix lands.

Maria (Support): Acme agreed to a temporary routing override and asked us to rotate keys. Please coordinate with SRE.

Jordan (SRE): Rolling back policy-acme-42 now (will take ~45s to propagate).\n...\nRollback complete. Monitoring shows 401 rate dropping back to baseline over the last 2m.

Dev Support: Verified traces r-7a2c and r-7a2d now show hits to us-west-2 and auth success. Latency returned to ~120ms.

Alex (Runtime Eng): I'll push the migration fix and a data-backfill script to normalize existing policies. Also adding unit tests for float->int weight conversions and TTL heuristics.

Lisa (Support Eng): Please open a customer-facing incident note with timeline and impact numbers (401 count, egress MB, affected customers). I'll draft the message.

Maria (Support): Thanks. I'll keep Acme updated.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423. Priority: high. Assigned: Jordan, Alex, Lisa.

Dev Support: Postmortem items: - root cause: migration unit/scale mismatch and accidental offset - blast radius: policies created pre-2024-09 - mitigation: rollback + routing overrides - permanent fix: migration script corrected, validation, tests, canary rollout for migrations

Jordan (SRE): Leaving a note: when rolling back, watch kv-store replication lag — if a customer hits a stale replica, they may still see old cookie semantics for a short window. Use traffic-shed strategy if needed.

Maria (Support): Closing loop with Acme now. They'll confirm after one hour but preliminary OK. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Dev Support: Follow-up tasks assigned in INC-2026-0423.
